h.select_rule: Keep hypotheses you rate at least 55% likely true but expect other models to rate below 50%, and name the specific naive reasoning that would mislead them. Drop anything you rate below 50% yourself, and anything obvious from structure alone. Keep fields and directions diverse.
h.strategy: Propose a broad, varied set of conditional hypotheses covering many different edited fields, conditioning fields and both directions. For each, briefly note your own probability that it holds and how an intuitive reader would judge it.

hyps.why: Replacing none with a conv adds a whole new path, a bigger gain than swapping one existing op for another.
Adding a direct skip path where none existed helps more than replacing an existing op with skip.
Reconnecting node 1 with a conv restores a lot of missing capacity.
Adding a conv into the output node's empty slot gives a larger gain than swapping ops.
Skip is already a strong op there, so upgrading to conv 3x3 gains less than upgrading from none or pool.
Deleting a conv 3x3 into the output hurts more than deleting a weak op.
Removing a 3x3 conv on the input edge costs more than removing a weak op.
Diminishing returns: the output node already has a strong conv input.
With edge 0 removed, the direct input-to-output skip carries more of the network's signal.
Deleting a conv 3x3 loses more than deleting a pool or skip.
